howItWorks.title: How MCP tool execution works in Neuron Runner
howItWorks.subtitle: Three layers ensure your tokens stay secure while giving frontier models autonomous capabilities.

step1.title: Encrypted Credential Vault
step1.description: Your OAuth tokens and API keys are encrypted at rest with Fernet cryptography. They are attached only to validated server-side MCP requests and never logged or exposed to the model.

step2.title: Validated Remote Gateway
step2.description: Remote MCP servers are reached through a validated HTTPS gateway with encrypted credentials and workspace-scoped authorization.

step3.title: Autonomous Model Calling
step3.description: Reasoning models discover available tool schemas automatically. The agent queries databases, pulls API specs, and applies fixes with full diff review controls.

q1.question: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
q1.answer: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that allows frontier AI models to discover, read, and invoke tools, databases, and APIs in a secure, standardized format. Rather than hardcoding custom integrations for every service, MCP enables universal plug-and-play tool calling.

q2.question: How do connectors run safely inside Neuron Runner?
q2.answer: Neuron Runner validates and proxies remote MCP sessions over HTTPS. Credentials stay encrypted on the server and are never exposed to the model or browser; the built-in browser runs inside your isolated workspace sandbox.

q3.question: How are my API tokens and OAuth credentials secured?
q3.answer: Your OAuth tokens and API keys are encrypted at rest with Fernet cryptography. They are attached only to validated server-side MCP requests and never logged or exposed to the model.

q4.question: Can I connect my own custom or private internal MCP server?
q4.answer: Yes. You can add any remote HTTP/SSE MCP endpoint from Integrations. Local stdio commands are no longer supported.

q5.question: Does Neuron Runner charge extra fees for using connectors?
q5.answer: No. All connectors and MCP servers are completely free to use with zero platform markup. You only pay standard per-second compute rates when your sandbox Docker container is actively executing.
